title: People Who End in CIAN
kidRule: When a 'shun' ending names a person and their job, it is spelled C-I-A-N. Look for the smaller word inside: MUSIC + IAN makes MUSICIAN, and MAGIC + IAN makes MAGICIAN. The C is already there!
hint: This word names a person with a job. The ending sounds like 'shun', but it is not T-I-O-N this time. Think of the smaller word hiding inside.
reminder: When 'shun' names a person, spell it C-I-A-N.

check.question: Why does MUSICIAN end with C-I-A-N?
check.correctAnswer: It names a person, and the C from MUSIC stays: MUSIC + IAN!
distractors: Because every word that ends in 'shun' is spelled C-I-A-N
Because words about music are not allowed to have a T

words.def: A person who does tricks that look impossible.
words.sent: The magician pulled a rabbit out of an empty hat.
words.story: A famous magician named Harry Houdini could wriggle out of handcuffs and locked trunks in front of huge crowds!
words.card: The *magician* did a *magic* trick and turned his hat into a pancake!

words.def: A person who plays an instrument or sings.
words.sent: The musician played a happy tune on her violin.
words.story: Mozart was a musician almost from the start: he began writing his own tunes when he was about five years old!
words.card: The *musician* played *music* on a banana trumpet!

words.def: A person whose job is to put in and fix wires, lights, and plugs.
words.sent: The electrician fixed the light in our hallway.
words.story: The first part of this word comes from 'elektron', the Greek word for amber. Long ago people noticed that rubbing amber makes it pull on feathers and dust!
words.card: The *electrician* fixed my *electric* toothbrush, and now it sings!

words.def: A person who makes and fits eyeglasses.
words.sent: The optician helped me choose bright green glasses.
words.story: The first eyeglasses were made in Italy more than 700 years ago. They had no arms, so people held them up or balanced them on their noses!
words.card: The *optician* gave the *tic*klish owl a pair of glasses!

words.def: A person who is skilled at working with machines or science tools.
words.sent: A technician repaired the school computer in ten minutes.
words.story: The first part of this word comes from 'techne', a Greek word that means skill or craft!
words.card: The *technician* fixed the robot at our pic*nic*!

words.def: A person who is chosen by voters to help run a town, state, or country.
words.sent: The politician promised to build a new playground.
words.story: This word grew from 'polis', the Greek word for a city. In ancient Greece, each city ran itself like a tiny country!
words.card: The *polit*e *politician* shook hands with every duck in the pond!

words.def: A person whose job is to cut and style hair and care for skin and nails.
words.sent: The beautician braided my hair with silver ribbons.
words.story: This word is only about a hundred years old. It was made up in America in the 1920s!
words.card: The *beautician* gave the poodle a *beaut*iful purple hairdo!

words.def: A doctor who helps sick people get well.
words.sent: The physician listened to my heartbeat and smiled.
words.story: Hippocrates was a physician in ancient Greece about 2,400 years ago. He is often called the father of medicine!
words.card: The *physician* told the sneezy guitar player to rest and play soft mu*sic*!

words.def: A person who is an expert with numbers, shapes, and patterns.
words.sent: The mathematician solved the puzzle with a pencil and a smile.
words.story: Katherine Johnson was a mathematician at NASA. Her careful sums helped astronauts fly to the moon and come home safely!
words.card: The *mathematician* did *math* on the back of a pizza box!

words.def: A doctor who takes care of babies and children.
words.sent: My pediatrician gave me a sticker after my checkup.
words.story: The first part of this word comes from the Greek word for child, so the whole word means a healer of children!
words.card: The *pediatrician* read an encyclo*pedia* to a teddy bear!
